subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Federal Shariat Court was established in:
explanation: Zia-ul-Haq created the Federal Shariat Court in 1980 by inserting Chapter 3-A into the Constitution.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The main function of the Federal Shariat Court is to examine whether:
o: A public servant has been corrupt
A law is repugnant to the injunctions of Islam
A province has breached the Constitution
explanation: The Court can strike down laws, or parts of laws, that it finds contrary to the Qur'an and Sunnah.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Besides judges qualified to be High Court judges, the Federal Shariat Court may include up to three members who are:
explanation: Article 203-C allows up to eight Muslim judges, of whom not more than three may be ulema with expertise in Islamic law.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Appeals against decisions of the Federal Shariat Court are heard by the:
o: Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court
explanation: The Shariat Appellate Bench, including ulema judges, hears appeals from the Federal Shariat Court.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In its judgment of April 2022, the Federal Shariat Court directed that riba be eliminated from the economy by the end of:
explanation: The Court declared interest-based laws un-Islamic and gave the government five years, until 31 December 2027, to move to an interest-free system.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Elections to the National Assembly, the Provincial Assemblies and the Senate are conducted by the:
explanation: Article 219 entrusts the Election Commission with preparing electoral rolls and organising general, Senate and by-elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Election Commission of Pakistan consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and:
o: Four members, one from each province
Seven members nominated by the President
explanation: Since the 18th Amendment the Commission comprises the CEC and four members, one from each province.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President after the Prime Minister consults:
o: The Leader of the Opposition, with confirmation by a parliamentary committee
explanation: Article 213 requires the Prime Minister and Leader of the Opposition to agree on names, which a bipartisan parliamentary committee then confirms.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for a term of:
explanation: Article 215 fixes the CEC's term at five years from the day he enters office.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Delimitation of constituencies for national and provincial elections is carried out by the:
explanation: The ECP draws constituency boundaries after each census under the Elections Act 2017.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Council of Common Interests is chaired by the:
explanation: Since the 18th Amendment, the Prime Minister chairs the CCI, which brings the federal and provincial governments together.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Besides the Prime Minister and the four Chief Ministers, the Council of Common Interests includes:
o: The Chief Justice and the Attorney-General
Three members nominated by the Federal Government
explanation: Article 153 provides for the Prime Minister, the Chief Ministers and three federal nominees.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Council of Common Interests formulates and regulates policies on matters in:
o: The Fourth Schedule's Part I only
Part II of the Federal Legislative List
explanation: Under Article 154, the CCI oversees subjects in Part II of the Federal Legislative List, such as railways, electricity and major industries.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After the 18th Amendment, the Council of Common Interests must meet at least once every:
explanation: Article 154 requires the CCI to meet at least once in ninety days and gave it a permanent secretariat.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: A province's complaint that its water supply from a natural source is being affected by another province is decided by the:
explanation: Article 155 lets a province complain to the CCI about interference with water supplies, and the CCI's decision is binding.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The National Finance Commission is chaired by the:
explanation: The NFC comprises the federal Finance Minister as chairman, the four provincial Finance Ministers and other members.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The main function of the National Finance Commission is to recommend:
o: Distribution of revenues between the Federation and the provinces
explanation: The NFC recommends how the divisible pool of federal taxes is shared between the centre and the provinces, and among the provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The National Finance Commission is constituted at intervals not exceeding:
explanation: Article 160 requires the President to set up the NFC at least every five years.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the 7th NFC Award (2009), the provinces' share of the divisible pool was raised to:
explanation: The 7th Award raised the provinces' combined share to 56 per cent in its first year and 57.5 per cent thereafter.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 7th NFC Award was the first to distribute resources among the provinces using, besides population:
o: Poverty, revenue generation and inverse population density
explanation: Earlier awards used population alone; the 7th Award gave weight to poverty or backwardness, revenue collection and inverse population density.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The National Accountability Bureau was established under the National Accountability Ordinance of:
explanation: Musharraf's government issued the National Accountability Ordinance in November 1999, creating NAB.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: NAB replaced the earlier accountability body known as the:
explanation: The Ehtesab Bureau set up under Nawaz Sharif's Ehtesab Act of 1997 was replaced by NAB in 1999.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Auditor-General of Pakistan is appointed by the:
explanation: Article 168 provides for the appointment of the Auditor-General by the President.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Auditor-General of Pakistan is responsible for auditing:
o: The accounts of the Federation and the provinces
explanation: The Auditor-General audits the public accounts of the federal and provincial governments and bodies they control.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Auditor-General's reports on the accounts of the Federation are submitted to the:
o: Prime Minister, who keeps them confidential
President, who has them laid before the National Assembly
explanation: Article 171 sends federal audit reports to the President to be laid before the National Assembly, where the PAC examines them.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Federal Ombudsman) was established in:
explanation: The Wafaqi Mohtasib was created by a President's Order in 1983 to redress complaints against federal agencies.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Wafaqi Mohtasib (Federal Ombudsman) deals with complaints of:
o: Violations of Islamic injunctions by laws
explanation: The Ombudsman investigates injustice caused by maladministration, such as delay or neglect, in federal departments.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The principal law officer of the Federal Government is the:
explanation: Under Article 100 the President appoints an Attorney-General to advise the Federal Government on legal matters; Advocates-General serve the provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Federal Public Service Commission is provided for under Article:
explanation: Article 242 provides for a public service commission for recruitment to federal services; Article 240 concerns terms of service.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Members of the Council of Islamic Ideology are appointed by the:
explanation: Article 228 provides that the President appoints the members of the Council, taking care to represent different schools of thought.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Council of Islamic Ideology consists of not less than eight and not more than:
explanation: Article 228 fixes the Council's strength at between eight and twenty members, including at least one woman.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The recommendations of the Council of Islamic Ideology are:
o: Enforced by the Federal Shariat Court automatically
Advisory, made to Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies
Final unless the Supreme Court overturns them
explanation: The CII advises legislatures on bringing laws into conformity with Islam; unlike the Federal Shariat Court, it cannot strike down laws.
